√श्रु (svādi 5 ‘to hear’, stem शृणु-), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada (an epic use; classical Sanskrit has the parasmaipada शृणु)

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi inside a compound (yaṇ and savarṇa-dīrgha)
sandhi.note: i before ā becomes y (वि + आहत → व्याहत); a + ā → ā (व्याहत + आज्ञा → व्याहताज्ञ).
Twice a + a → ā: निर्जिताखिल, दैत्यारि.

sandhi.type: visarga sandhi (special rule for सः); consonant sandhi (voicing)
sandhi.note: The visarga of सः is dropped before the consonant y; the final t of यत् becomes d before the vowel of आह.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (its first member अव्याहत is a nañ tatpuruṣa: न व्याहता)
samasa.literal: one whose command is not struck down
samasa.sense: a ruler whose orders no one resists

samasa.literal: among the kinds (births) of the gods
samasa.sense: among all the orders of superhuman beings
samasa.alt: देवयोनि is often a bahuvrīhi, देवः योनिः येषां ते ‘beings of divine origin’ (masculine). Here the feminine सर्वासु shows that योनि ‘kind, birth’ (f.) is the head, so the tatpuruṣa fits.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (inside it दैत्यारि is a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, दैत्यानाम् अरिः)
samasa.literal: one by whom all the Daitya-enemies have been conquered
samasa.sense: the conqueror of all the gods
samasa.alt: दैत्यारि ‘enemy of the Daityas’ can name Viṣṇu alone; with अखिल ‘all’ the whole body of gods is meant.

morph.note: √ब्रू has in the present the substitute आह with perfect-type endings (आह, आहतुः, आहुः); Pāṇini allows it optionally beside ब्रवीति. The sense is present: ‘(he) says’.
Imperative ātmanepada of √श्रु. The root is parasmaipada in Pāṇini; the ātmanepada imperative is common in the epics and Purāṇas, with no difference of sense.
The feminine आज्ञा is shortened to आज्ञ as the last member of a bahuvrīhi that qualifies a masculine: ‘he whose command …’.

mantras.anvaya: यः सदा सर्वासु देवयोनिषु अव्याहताज्ञः, निर्जिताखिलदैत्यारिः सः (शुम्भः) यत् आह, तत् शृणुष्व।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (यः … अव्याहताज्ञः) and a second epithet describe the subject सः; inside the main clause a second relative pair (यत् … तत्) makes the object of the imperative शृणुष्व.
mantras.lit: He who always (has) unobstructed command among all the divine orders, (and) who has conquered all the enemies of the Daityas — hear that which he says.
mantras.tr: Among all the orders of heavenly beings his command is never resisted, and he has vanquished every foe of the Daityas. Hear what he says.
mantras.tr_note: The relative clause is turned into two plain statements.

comm.t: The messenger Sugrīva, sent by Śumbha (5.102–104), finishes introducing his master (5.106) before delivering the message. The two titles summarise the opening of the chapter: the brothers have taken the gods’ offices and driven them out (5.2–5).

देवयोनि is the usual name for the superhuman orders below the gods proper; the lexicon Amarakośa lists ten (vidyādharas, apsarases, yakṣas, rakṣases, gandharvas, kinnaras, piśācas, guhyakas, siddhas and bhūtas). The claim is that every such order obeys Śumbha.
A modern reading: the message is preceded by credentials. Power announces itself before it asks, so that the asking sounds like a favour.

indeclinable (adverb)

sandhi.type: no change before a vowel; anusvāra sandhi
sandhi.note: Final m stays m before the vowel of अखिलम् and is simply written with it; before the consonant of मम it becomes anusvāra.
-āḥ before a voiced sound: the visarga becomes y and the y is dropped, leaving -ā.

sandhi.type: no change (final n before a vowel)
sandhi.rule: ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम् (8.3.32) does not apply
sandhi.note: The n is not doubled, because the vowel before it (ā) is long; it is simply joined to अहम्. The same in सर्वानुपाश्नामि.

samasa.sense: the offerings due to each god at the rite

samasa.vigraha: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः त्रिलोकी, सा एव त्रैलोक्यम्
samasa.type: samāhāra dvigu (त्रिलोकी), made into a noun with the taddhita ṣyañ that adds no new sense
samasa.sense: the whole universe: earth, the middle region and heaven

morph.note: √अश् ‘to eat’ belongs to the ninth class: अश् + ना → अश्नामि. With उप the prefix and the root vowel merge (उप + अश्नामि → उपाश्नामि). The verb of eating is chosen for the sacrificial shares, which the gods ‘eat’.
The repeated adverb (पृथक् पृथक्) expresses distribution, ‘one by one, each share apart’ — every god’s portion now goes to Śumbha.

mantras.anvaya: अखिलं त्रैलोक्यं मम (अस्ति); देवाः मम वशानुगाः (सन्ति); अहं सर्वान् यज्ञभागान् पृथक् पृथक् उपाश्नामि।
mantras.anvaya_en: Three clauses, the first two nominal (the verb ‘is / are’ understood), the third with the finite verb उपाश्नामि. From here to 5.114 the messenger speaks in Śumbha’s first person.
mantras.lit: Mine is the entire triple world; mine are the gods, following my will. All the shares of the sacrifice I enjoy, each separately.
mantras.tr: “The three worlds are mine entire, and the gods obey my will. Every share of the sacrifice, one by one, is mine to enjoy.
mantras.tr_note: The opening quotation mark shows that the message is quoted in Śumbha’s own words.

comm.t: The message proper begins, in Śumbha’s voice. Its claims repeat the narrator’s account at the head of the chapter: the three worlds and the sacrificial shares were taken from Indra (5.2), and the gods were driven out (5.4–5).

The sacrificial share (यज्ञभाग) is the gods’ sustenance and the sign of their office. In the Purāṇic view, a demon who eats the shares has overturned the order of the world, not merely won a war; the Devī’s own message in 8.26 demands that the gods again be ‘eaters of oblations’ (हविर्भुजः), and 12.34 records that they enjoyed their shares once more.

sandhi.note: Final i before a different vowel becomes y.

samasa.sense: the finest treasures of every kind
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, रत्नानां वराणि ‘the best of jewels’; the sense is the same.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (of selection: ‘the jewel among elephants’)
samasa.sense: the finest of elephants, Airāvata (named in 5.94)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, whose first member is also a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa
samasa.literal: the vehicle of the chief of the gods

morph.note: Absolutive of √हृ (no prefix, so -त्वा, not -य). It has no finite verb of its own in the verse: the sense ‘(is mine), having been seized by me’ is carried over from मम वश्यानि. A loose construction typical of reported speech.
वश ‘control’ + the taddhita -य: ‘what is in (one’s) control’. With the genitive मम: ‘subject to me’.

mantras.anvaya: त्रैलोक्ये (यानि) वररत्नानि (तानि) अशेषतः मम वश्यानि (सन्ति); तथा एव देवेन्द्रवाहनं गजरत्नं च (मया) हृत्वा (मम वश्यम्)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line is a nominal sentence (verb understood). The second hangs on the absolutive हृत्वा and borrows its predicate from the first: the elephant too is ‘subject to me’.
mantras.lit: In the three worlds the choice jewels are subject to me without exception; and likewise the jewel of elephants, the mount of the lord of the gods, having seized (it) —
mantras.tr: Every treasure of worth in the three worlds belongs to me, without exception — so too the king of elephants, Indra’s own mount, which I have taken.
mantras.tr_note: The absolutive हृत्वा is rendered as a relative clause ‘which I have taken’, completing the loose syntax.

comm.t: Śumbha’s message repeats what Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa told him (5.93–94): the jewels of the three worlds are in his palace, and Indra’s elephant Airāvata among them. The messenger turns their report into a boast.

रत्न ‘jewel’ in this passage means the best of any kind — elephant, horse, tree, woman — not only gems. The list prepares the inference of 5.112: if all jewels are his, the ‘jewel of women’ must be his too.

words.en: that arose from the churning of the Milk Ocean

first-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg., used for the dative (recipient) with समर्पितम्
m. instr. pl. of अमर; agent of समर्पितम्
n. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies अश्वरत्नम्

absolutive (lyap) of प्र + नि + √पत् (bhvādi 1P ‘to fall’); its subject is the agent अमरैः
past passive participle (kta) of सम् + √ऋ, causative stem अर्पय-, n. nom. sg.; predicate

sandhi.type: no change before a vowel; anusvāra sandhi
sandhi.note: Final m is joined to the vowel of अश्वरत्नम्; the m of अश्वरत्नम् becomes anusvāra before मम.
Final t stays unvoiced before the unvoiced p; the words are only written together.

samasa.type: pañcamī tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (क्षीरोदमथन)
samasa.literal: arisen from the churning of the milk-water (ocean)
samasa.sense: one of the treasures that came up when gods and asuras churned the ocean
samasa.alt: क्षीरोद itself is a bahuvrīhi, क्षीरम् उदकं यस्य सः ‘that whose water is milk’, with उदक shortened to उद.
The name उच्चैःश्रवस् is itself a bahuvrīhi, उच्चैः श्रवसी यस्य सः ‘whose ears are high’ (or ‘whose neigh is loud’).

morph.note: Past passive participle of the causative of सम् + √ऋ (‘cause to go to’ = ‘hand over’): सम्-अर्पित. With the instrumental अमरैः it is a passive sentence: ‘(it) was surrendered by the gods’.
Absolutive with prefixes, so -य (lyap). In a passive sentence its subject is the agent in the instrumental: the gods bowed, then handed over the horse.

The horse’s name is the s-stem उच्चैःश्रवस्; in this compound it appears as उच्चैःश्रवस-, as if an a-stem, a by-form found in epic and Purāṇic usage. The visarga of उच्चैः is kept inside the compound, as printed.

mantras.anvaya: क्षीरोदमथनोद्भूतम् उच्चैःश्रवससंज्ञं तत् अश्वरत्नम् अमरैः प्रणिपत्य मम समर्पितम्।
mantras.anvaya_en: A passive sentence: subject अश्वरत्नम् with three qualifiers, agent अमरैः, recipient मम, predicate समर्पितम्; the absolutive प्रणिपत्य belongs to the agent.
mantras.lit: That jewel of horses called Uccaiḥśravas, which arose from the churning of the Milk Ocean, was handed over to me by the immortals, having bowed down.
mantras.tr: Uccaiḥśravas, the finest of horses, born from the churning of the Ocean of Milk, the gods themselves surrendered to me with bowed heads.

comm.t: The second of Indra’s great treasures: the horse Uccaiḥśravas, already listed by Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa (5.94). Śumbha adds a detail they did not give — the gods bowed as they handed it over.

Uccaiḥśravas is one of the treasures that rose from the ocean when the gods and asuras churned it, and belongs to Indra in the Purāṇic accounts. A treasure won by the gods from that churning is now given up to an asura: the boast measures how complete his victory is.

words.g: n. nom. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies भूतानि
n. nom. pl. of भूत (noun: ‘what has come to be’); subject of the relative clause
pronoun तद्, n. nom. pl.; correlative of यानि; subject of the main clause
first-person pronoun अस्मद्, loc. sg.

f. voc. sg. of शोभना (√शुभ् + lyuṭ, ‘shining, lovely’); addresses the Devī

sandhi.note: The final i of मयि becomes y before e, so the y of the stem and the new y stand together (मय्येव).

samasa.literal: that have become jewels, that are jewels
samasa.sense: treasures of the first rank among their kind

morph.note: The same word stands twice in a row with two functions: in रत्नभूतानि ‘being jewels’ it is the participle of √भू; alone, भूतानि is the noun ‘things, beings’. The play (रत्नभूतानि भूतानि) is deliberate: ‘things that are jewels’.
Vocative of the feminine शोभना: the -ā stem has -e in the vocative singular. The flattering address prepares the proposal of 5.112.

mantras.anvaya: शोभने, देवेषु गन्धर्वेषु उरगेषु च यानि च अन्यानि रत्नभूतानि भूतानि (सन्ति), तानि मयि एव (सन्ति)।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (यानि … भूतानि) names the subject; the main clause तानि मयि एव is nominal, with ‘are’ understood.
mantras.lit: And whatever other things that are jewels (there are) among the gods, the Gandharvas and the serpents — they (are) in me alone, O beautiful one.
mantras.tr: And whatever else ranks as a jewel among gods, Gandharvas and serpents — all of it, lovely one, rests with me alone.

comm.t: The list of treasures closes with a general claim: every ‘jewel’ of every race is now in Śumbha’s possession. The vocative शोभने turns the boast towards the Devī.
The Devī is addressed first as ‘beautiful’; in the next verse she is placed among the jewels. The argument is the one Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa made (5.100): all jewels are his, so why not this one?
